sources.citation: Keegan, John M. 2014. The Central Sara Languages. 9th ed. Cuenca: Morkeg Books (Sara Language Project), 505 pp. Includes 'Transcription for the Sara Languages' (printed pp. 6-15) and Kosmadji Merci, Etienne Odjiadoum & John M. Keegan, 'Lexique Gor' with 'Introduction to the Gor Lexicon' (printed pp. 101-109).

sources.note: Nothing. General section states all Sara languages have three even tones (high, mid, low), contour tones on identical-vowel sequences and sonorant codas (p. 10); the Gor introduction ('Comments on the Phonology', vowel patterns, sound changes, tone loss of neutralized vowels) never mentions stress, accent or prominence (a full-text search for stress/accent full text + read of both sections).
